markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize **recency-balanced cutoff sampling**, a small, controlled change to the supplied BERT4Rec.

**Insights.** From the starting point: (1) separately normalized reconstruction and terminal losses preserve explicit coefficient balance despite different target counts; (2) prefix truncation prevents bidirectional target leakage; (3) holding full-history endpoint probability at 0.1 isolates changes in nonterminal recency. From related work: (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) motivates examining reconstruction versus appended-mask prediction; (2) [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates emphasizing recent prediction contexts, without establishing gains here; (3) [PCGrad](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782) provides a conflict diagnostic, but these objectives have no measured gradient conflict yet.

The user diagnosis identifies broad associations displacing specific current interests and historical purchases implying persistent demand. Recent terminal targets could improve sensitivity to changing preferences and reduce stale, redundant recommendations; these are hypotheses, not observed improvements. Industrial/Electronics have negative lower-tail margins (−0.1487/−0.2356), motivating better terminal discrimination. Their lower user RankMe does not establish collapse.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Gap / proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Masked reconstruction | Separately normalized terminal supervision |
| Temporal relevance | Uniform cutoffs | Recent/uniform cutoff mixture |
| Optimization | Shared loss sum | Measure conflict before projection |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Assessments |
|---|---|
| **A: Recent/uniform cutoffs** [Recency Sampling] | O 4: +controlled combination, −incremental; P 7: +cheap foundation, −recency may mislead; U 7: +targets stale demand and present-preference mismatch, −needs remain latent; M 7: +terminal discrimination, −unverified; D 2: +sampler-only, −endpoint bookkeeping |
| B: Terminal-only objective [BERT4Rec] | O 3: +clean alignment, −established concept; P 6: +simple control, −loses reconstruction; U 6: +next-choice emphasis, −no explicit compatibility; M 7: +direct separation, −less supervision; D 2: +one branch, −budget matching |
| C: Conflict-conditioned projection [PCGrad] | O 4: +task-specific application, −existing algorithm; P 5: +protects conflicting gradients, −conflict unmeasured; U 4: +indirect relevance, −weak intent link; M 5: +tests interference, −not concentration; D 6: +standard method, −extra backward cost |

**Selected experiment: A.** Establish the uniform control first. Sample target index `t=n−1` with probability 0.1; otherwise sample eligible nonterminal indices uniformly. The treatment changes only that conditional distribution to `0.5·Uniform(eligible)+0.5·Uniform(last ten eligible)`. For short histories, use available eligible indices; singleton eligibility requires an explicitly logged exception.

Terminal input is `history[:t]+[MASK]`, truncated to capacity; reconstruction uses a separate corrupted-history pass through the same network. Optimize `0.5·mean(CE_terminal)+0.5·mean(CE_reconstruction)`. Log actual cutoff probabilities and branch target counts. Preserve left-padding readout, predictor/checkpoint consistency, diagnostic interfaces, seeds, four-category routing, and one checkpoint/category. Select using host macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget; report margins and user rejection reasons separately.

idea.description: Change only the nonterminal cutoff distribution in the supplied jointly trained BERT4Rec: mix uniform eligible cutoffs and the most recent ten eligible cutoffs equally, while retaining a 0.1 probability of selecting the final training interaction.
idea.motivation: Test whether increased exposure to recent terminal prediction contexts addresses stale purchase-driven redundancy and mismatches with present content preferences. The model-facing hypothesis is improved terminal discrimination in Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics, where measured lower-tail training margins are negative. No validation improvement or causal explanation is established.
idea.implementation_notes: First establish the uniform-cutoff control with separately target-normalized losses weighted 0.5 each. Change only cutoff sampling for the treatment; retain the supplied architecture, optimizer, reconstruction policy, training seeds, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Eligible terminal targets require at least one preceding interaction. If exactly one eligible target exists, it must be selected with probability one; count this exception separately. Use training histories only, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Keep one independently trained checkpoint per category and all four routing paths. Preserve reserved MASK tokens, appended-mask inference, maximum-nonpadding-index readout, ModelView compatibility, DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt. Persist measured training counters alongside checkpoints so diagnostics do not infer branch allocations from loader coverage. No inference change is required for this sampler-only experiment.
idea.pseudocode:
def choose_target(history, rng, treatment):
    # Zero-based target indices; each target has preceding context.
    eligible = list(range(1, len(history)))
    if not eligible:
        return None
    if len(eligible) == 1:
        log_single_eligible_exception()
        return eligible[0]
    endpoint = eligible[-1]
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        return endpoint
    nonterminal = eligible[:-1]
    pool = nonterminal
    if treatment and rng.random() < 0.5:
        pool = nonterminal[-10:]
    return rng.choice(pool)

# Use the host's seeded RNG and unchanged reconstruction sampler.
# For every sampled terminal example:
t = choose_target(history, rng, treatment)
terminal_sequence = left_pad(history[:t][-(maxlen - 1):] + [MASK], maxlen)
terminal_target = history[t]
# The target occurrence and all subsequent events are absent.
terminal_loss = mean_valid_terminal_cross_entropy(model, terminal_batch)
reconstruction_loss = mean_valid_reconstruction_cross_entropy(model, reconstruction_batch)
loss = 0.5 * terminal_loss + 0.5 * reconstruction_loss
# Both passes update the same BERT4Rec parameters.
# Record branch target counts, coefficient masses, and sampled cutoff indices.
# Evaluate exclusively through the unchanged host validation protocol.

originality.positive: A controlled combination of endpoint-preserving sampling and recent nonterminal contexts makes the hypothesis easy to attribute.
originality.negative: Recency sampling and terminal-mask supervision are established ingredients; this is an incremental experiment.

future_potential.positive: A low-cost result could establish a useful sampling foundation before adding temporal features or optimization machinery.
future_potential.negative: Recent events can reflect completed purchases or temporary interests, so recency alone cannot establish unresolved need.

code_difficulty.positive: The treatment changes only target selection and leaves inference architecture unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Short-history exceptions, exact endpoint probability, and diagnostic bookkeeping require care.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the backbone and masked-target formulation retained in this experiment.
limitations: Interior reconstruction can exploit context unavailable during appended-mask next-item prediction.
Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed cutoff mixture on the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling
contributions: Motivates examining the relationship between masking, recent contexts, and next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not validate the exact endpoint-preserving mixture proposed here.
Reported findings cannot supply expected gains for these four datasets and this evaluator.

related_work.title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
contributions: Defines gradient conflict through negative dot products and proposes projection of conflicting gradient components.
Motivates measuring interference between reconstruction and terminal objectives.
limitations: No supplied measurement establishes gradient conflict between these BERT4Rec objectives.
Projection adds training cost and is deferred until conflict is measured.
